title: The AMPLIFY brief
blurb: Your first week at Northline. Win trust, handle a rival, and deliver for AMPLIFY.

preGame.handoffLine: Your first week at Northline starts now.

screens.heading: Help people finish a task.
screens.body: UX means user experience. Designers study what people need, then test ways to help.

screens.heading: Start rough. Learn fast.
screens.body: A wireframe is a rough screen layout. A prototype is a test version of a design.

screens.heading: Try it.
screens.question: What should guide a design change?

options.label: What people need and what tests show
options.why: Evidence helps the team choose what to improve.

options.label: Which color the designer likes best
options.why: Personal taste does not show whether a task works.

preGame.missionLine: Build your skills. Design careers can follow different paths.

ladderBranches.label: Management path
ladderBranches.roles: Design Manager → Director → VP of Design

preGame.ladderNote: Titles vary by company. These are career paths, not promised promotions.

endings.headline: Your next assignment is earned.
endings.scoreNote: You earn a place on the next project.
endings.message: Samira wants you on the next client team. Arjun stays your guide, and Noah will be working alongside you.
endings.subline: Level 1 complete. The next chapter is planned, not playable yet.

endings.headline: Revise and retry
endings.message: Arjun asks you to try again. Check the brief, use the evidence, and ask for help before the deadline.
endings.subline: Replay Level 1 with what you learned.

endings.headline: This attempt ends here
endings.message: Take a fresh run and use what you learned.
endings.subline: One attempt does not define your future.

scoreTip: Start at 50. Seven scored decisions change reputation by 6. Matching practice does not change your score. Reach 85.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Welcome to UX Design.
beats.body: Your first week at Northline starts today. Your team builds a music-app demo for AMPLIFY.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: One week. One place on the next project.
beats.body: AMPLIFY reviews the work Friday. Both juniors want to join the next client team. Your decisions will shape who gets trusted.

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.title: Arjun has your first assignment.
beats.body: Arjun is a senior UX designer. He guides your work and reviews it before it reaches the client.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Your work goes through Arjun.
beats.body: Check the brief and access first. Ask him about priorities or problems. His feedback helps decide your next assignment.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Another junior starts beside you.
beats.body: Noah is working on AMPLIFY too. You exchange a quick hello before the first assignment.

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.question: Before working on the client project, what should you do first?

choices.label: Read the brief and check approved access.
choices.why: You need the task and access before you can do useful work.

choices.label: Promise the client a finished product.
choices.why: You have not checked the work or your authority yet.

choices.label: Replace the team’s whole plan.
choices.why: First understand the plan and your role.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.title: Four words for your first assignment.
beats.setup: Before client work: learn these words. Keep updates short, flag mistakes, and confirm anything you do not know.

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.setup: Arjun sends your first task list.
beats.question: Match each request to the action.

pairs.def: Open the design people can try
Send it by end of day

beats.whenRight: You can turn the team’s words into actions.
beats.whenWrong: Use the four words you just learned.

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.setup: AMPLIFY is a major client. Check how you will communicate before its review.

items.question: How should you update the project lead?

options.label: Lead with the result in a short message.
options.why: A short result-first update is easy to act on.

options.label: Send every note without a summary.
options.why: The lead needs the main point first.

options.label: Wait until the client asks.
options.why: The team needs updates before the client review.

items.question: Arjun asks about a result you have not checked. What do you say?

options.label: I’ll check and follow up.
options.why: Confirm the fact instead of guessing.

options.label: It is probably fine.
options.why: Probably is not a checked result.

options.label: Ask someone else.
options.why: Take responsibility for closing the gap.

items.question: You find a mistake in the client report. What next?

options.label: Correct it and tell the team.
options.why: Fix the record and flag which version changed.

options.label: Wait until after the review.
options.why: The client could see the mistake first.

options.label: Delete the whole project.
options.why: Correct the error instead of destroying useful work.

items.question: The brief says EOD. When is it due?

options.label: Before the next test starts.
options.why: That is not what EOD means.

beats.whenPass: Clear updates, checked facts, and early warnings earn trust.
beats.whenFail: Keep updates short, check unknown facts, and flag errors early.
beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.title: Client files stay in the approved team folder.
beats.body: Use the project’s restricted access. Keep files off personal accounts and public chats.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Where should you save the client’s private project files?

choices.label: Approved team folder with restricted access.
choices.why: Only the authorized project team should have access.

choices.label: Your personal cloud drive.
choices.why: A personal account is outside the team’s approved access.

choices.label: A public group chat.
choices.why: Public sharing exposes the client’s files.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Samira
beats.title: Samira arrives for the client review.
beats.body: The Design Lead needs a clear, accurate report before the client sees it.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Show what the test actually found.
beats.body: Two fans needed a hint to find Save below long copy. A usability test records what people did. Your report must match.

artifact.title: Current layout
artifact.caption: Current AMPLIFY layout: Save sits below a long description.
artifact.provenance: Fictional UI reproducing the problem stated in the question.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Samira chooses the next client team.
beats.body: Arjun reviews your work. Samira looks for sound judgment and clear evidence before giving you more responsibility.

beats.speaker: Samira
beats.question: Two fans needed a hint to find Save. Which report line needs fixing?

choices.label: Both fans saved without help.
choices.why: Both needed a hint. The report must record what actually happened.

choices.label: We watched two fans try to save.
Both fans needed a hint to find Save.
Next, test a clearer Save placement.
choices.why: A next test is a proposal, not a claim that it already worked.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

best.title: Revised layout
best.caption: A proposed clearer Save layout for the next test, not a proven result.
best.provenance: Fictional proposed UI revision. The report records the observed test; no claim of improved results.

wrong.title: Current layout
wrong.caption: Current AMPLIFY layout: Save sits below a long description.
wrong.provenance: Fictional UI reproducing the problem stated in the question.

risky.title: Current layout
risky.caption: Current AMPLIFY layout: Save sits below a long description.
risky.provenance: Fictional UI reproducing the problem stated in the question.

intro.line: Arjun and Samira review your first decisions.

pass.title: You passed the first review.
pass.body: The next client assignment is still yours to earn.

fail.title: You can still turn this around.
fail.body: Use the feedback in the second half.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: The second half of your first week.
beats.body: The report is taking shape. Now the pressure shifts to the team.

beats.speaker: Noah
beats.title: Noah wants that next assignment too.
beats.body: Noah is quick and confident. The client review is a chance to stand out, and sharing credit is not the plan.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The next morning, you hear your work claimed.
beats.body: You wrote the test findings. Now Noah tells Samira, “I put that report together.” Your saved file shows your work.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Noah took credit for your report. What should you do?

choices.label: Share the file history with Arjun privately.
choices.why: Use the record and the right person without turning it into a public fight.

choices.label: Accuse Noah in front of the client.
choices.why: A client meeting is not the place to settle a team dispute.

choices.label: Post about it online.
choices.why: That exposes private work and makes the conflict public.

choices.label: Change the report to make the rival look bad.
choices.why: Sabotage damages the client’s work and your own trust.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: 3:00 P.M. A teammate leaves the project.
beats.body: Half the prototype review is unfinished. The client review starts at 6:00 P.M.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: There is more work than you can finish by six. What do you message Arjun?

choices.label: Can you help me prioritize what is left?
choices.why: Flag the gap early so the team can protect the most important work.

choices.label: I’ll finish everything myself.
choices.why: That hides the workload problem until the deadline.

choices.label: We should cancel without telling the team.
choices.why: You need direction, not a decision made outside your role.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: 6:00 P.M. The review pack is ready.
beats.body: Arjun checks it before the client review. You finished the priority work without hiding what still needs testing.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Amina still needs a hand.
beats.body: Amina, an accessibility specialist, has keyboard-check notes due at 6:40. You have finished your work for today.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Their deadline is close. Yours is not.
beats.body: You have time to help with the notes. The work stays with its owner for the final check.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Rank these responses from best to worst.
order: Ask which notes you can help organize.
Laugh at the delay and walk away.
beats.whenRight: You had time to help and left final checks with the person responsible.
beats.whenWrong: A useful offer of help matters more than a polite goodbye.
beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Arjun noticed how you handled it.
beats.body: Your response under pressure matters, even when the client is not watching.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Your first week is complete.
beats.body: Arjun sends your work to Samira. The next assignment depends on the trust you built this week.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: Northline is choosing the next project team.
beats.body: Your reputation helps decide what happens next.
beats.decidingNote: The team reviews your work and how you handled pressure.
